questions.question: Basket A contains 1 apple and 2 oranges. Basket B contains 1 banana and 1 mango. A fruit is picked at random from each basket. **(i)** Draw a tree diagram to show all possible outcomes. **(ii)** Write the sample space $S$ and find $n(S)$. **(iii)** What is the probability of picking an apple and a banana?

solution.content: **(i) Tree diagram:** First branch from Basket A: Apple, Orange, Orange. From each of these, second branches from Basket B: Banana, Mango.
**(ii) Sample space:** Each outcome is a pair (fruit from A, fruit from B): $$S = \{(\text{Apple, Banana}), (\text{Apple, Mango}), (\text{Orange, Banana}), (\text{Orange, Mango})\}, \quad n(S) = 4$$
**(iii) Probability of apple and banana:** Only 1 outcome is (Apple, Banana) out of 4 total outcomes: $$P(\text{apple and banana}) = \frac{1}{4}$$

formulaBox.title: Tree Diagram
formulaBox.content: Multiply along the branches to count outcomes: $n(S) = 3 \times 2 = 6$ paths, but here Basket A has 2 distinct fruits (Apple, Orange) so $n(S) = 2 \times 2 = 4$.

questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** A tree diagram helps list outcomes systematically without missing any.

questions.question: A box contains 3 red, 4 black, and 2 green pens. A pen is picked at random, its colour is noted, and it is put back. Then another pen is picked. **(i)** Write the sample space $S$ for this experiment. **(ii)** What is the probability that both pens are of the same colour?

solution.content: **(i) Sample space (with replacement):** Each outcome is an ordered pair (first colour, second colour): $$S = \{(R,R), (R,B), (R,G), (B,R), (B,B), (B,G), (G,R), (G,B), (G,G)\}, \quad n(S) = 9$$
**(ii) Probability of same colour:** Favourable outcomes: $(R,R), (B,B), (G,G)$ — that is 3 outcomes. $$P(\text{same colour}) = \frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}$$

questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** 'With replacement' means the first pen is returned, so the second pick has the same 3-colour options — giving $3 \times 3 = 9$ outcomes.
